parole.significato: a dry measure equivalent to 11.7 litres, divided into six almuds in Mallorca and four in the Valencian Community
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Mozarabic descendant of Late Latin particella, diminutive of Latin particula. The change from /p-/ to /b-/ would be the result of Arabic influence.

parole.significato: reamer, auger, gimlet (tool for boring holes)
parole.testo: From Mozarabic barrina, from Late Latin veruīna (“long javelin”), from Latin veru (“spit, javelin”). Cognate with Spanish barrena.

The GDLC derive it from Mozarabic 'iškaylûla, diminutive of escalla, from Late Latin scandula (“type of wheat”). (Compare Spanish escanda (“emmer wheat”).) The DCVB derive it from Late Latin ēscāriola (“endive plant”), also the source of Catalan escarola.

parole.significato: a coot, especially a Eurasian coot (Fulica atra)
parole.testo: Perhaps borrowed from a Mozarabic *folğa, *folec̆a, from Latin fulicem, variant of fulica.
From earlier *pissaptot by metathesis, and this in turn from Mozarabic pissabt, from Latin pisum sapidum (“tasty pea”).
Borrowed from Mozarabic *bardiláqa, from Latin portulāca, with influence from verd.

Borrowed from Mozarabic *činče, itself from Latin cīmicem (cf. Spanish chinche). The Catalan singular xinxa is a back-formation from the plural xinxes. Displaced Old Catalan címeu, which was directly inherited from Latin.
From Mozarabic *atxorriiaka, from a metathesised version of Vulgar Latin *excorrigiata, from corrigia (“thong; whip”).
Borrowed from Mozarabic číčaro, from Latin cicer (“chickpea”). Cognate with Spanish chícharo.
